newsitem.title: CHINA: China blasts Japan war shrine as 'road to ruin'.
newsitem.headline: China blasts Japan war shrine as 'road to ruin'.

text.p: China slammed on Monday a plan by a Japanese group to build a shrine to soldiers killed in World War Two, saying the temple would not reflect the suffering Japan's imperial army inflicted on its Asian neighbours.
The plan by a right-wing Japanese group to build the new war shrine to Japan's fallen troops could lead Tokyo to repeat its ruinous wartime aggression, the official Guangming Daily said.
"This kind of thinking will unavoidably mislead a whole generation of Japanese and increase the danger that Japan will follow the same old road to ruin," the newspaper said.
The shrine would only highlight the difficulties Japanese soldiers and their families faced in the war while neglecting the suffering of Asian countries invaded by Japan, it said.
"It does not reflect Japan's invasion of Asian countries and peoples or its history of devastation," it said.
"How can Japan's neighbours be at ease when Japan has been acting the way it has the last several years?" the newspaper said.
China indignantly protested against a visit by several Japanese cabinet ministers to a shrine dedicated to Japan's war dead last August on the 51st anniversary of Japan's World War Two surrender.
Beijing has expressed concern over what it sees as resurgent militarism in Japan and accuses Tokyo of trying to whitewash its wartime atrocities.
China estimates up to 35 million Chinese were killed or wounded by invading Japanese troops from 1931 to 1945.
